findings.reason: The protected query is direct, conventional, and expert-interview ready. Its aliases expose the two source tables, its join follows the country identifier relationship, its inclusive date predicate isolates the exact target month, its grouping preserves country identity, and its CASE expression mirrors the three classification intervals without unnecessary CTEs or repeated work. No material solution improvement warrants a candidate.

Filtering before aggregation leaves exactly the November 2019 observations. The inner join attaches the unique country name to each retained identifier, and grouping by country_id and country_name forms one aggregate per qualifying country even when names repeat. The CASE branches partition every numeric average into at most 15, strictly between 15 and 25, or at least 25, so every emitted label is exact and a country without target-month data cannot appear.

An independent Python oracle filtered ISO dates, accumulated integer sums and counts by country_id, compared exact products against the 15 and 25 thresholds without floating-point rounding, and joined names only after classification. It, the protected app source, immutable native source, an independently written preaggregate-then-join query, and a slower correlated control agreed on all nine visible cases and all three benchmark tiers.

All 7,381 weather-state sequences of length zero through four over {-20, 0, 14, 15, 16, 24, 25, 26, 40} matched every implementation. Seed 1294 then generated 2,000 schema-valid databases with shuffled rows, 146 empty country tables, 154 empty weather tables, 1,623 databases with duplicate country names, 1,727 countries lacking November observations, 81,165 out-of-month rows, 59,762 negative observations, and outputs spanning 8,467 Cold, 1,017 Warm, and 940 Hot classifications.

The three tiers retain their original 32, 128, and 512 total-row sizes and 16x span. Across three real-test repetitions, the protected query passed every output and scaling verdict with extra growth exponent -0.02 through 0.00 and largest-tier ratio 1.00x through 1.01x; the independent preaggregate control was similarly stable. A correct correlated average passed all nine ordinary and three benchmark outputs but failed only scaling every time, at +0.58 through +0.61 extra exponent and 5.83x through 6.00x largest-tier ratio.

Authenticated source evidence explicitly permits any result order, but the hidden performance tiers previously used exact ordered-table comparison. Each tier now uses the unordered_table validator while retaining its input, expected row multiset, size, timeout, and workload. This prevents benchmark.json from acting as a hidden correctness-order test and leaves its scaling calibration intact.

The complete Approach now derives the join-filter-group pipeline, explains why country_id must remain in the grouping key, proves both directions of output membership and all three CASE intervals, and states the expected O(C+W) time and O(C) working space under hash join and aggregation. Its alternatives and edge cases cover preaggregation, correlated rescans, half-open dates, filter placement, duplicate names, exact thresholds, fractional and negative averages, missing November data, and unrestricted order.

All nine ordinary cases are visible samples or trials and use unordered-table comparison. The sole source example is first and now preserves the provider's exact input rows and output row order while correctly treating that order as nonbinding. Formerly hidden negative and endpoint cases are visible, and new trials cover completely empty tables plus distinct country identifiers sharing a name.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode database problem 1294 and SQL/MySQL as the native environment. The query respects both primary keys, uses only November 2019 rows, retains averages exactly at 15 and 25 in the Cold and Hot classes, respectively, omits countries without qualifying data, and returns only country_name and weather_type.

The protected app-local sql.sql and immutable leetcode.sql bound to verified submission 2068365190 remain byte-for-byte identical and unchanged, as does submission.json. Their join, date filter, grouping key, average thresholds, projected columns, labels, and deterministic presentation order are exactly aligned.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed both table schemas and primary keys, the November 2019 averaging task, all three inclusive/open classification rules, unrestricted result order, one example with its six-country and seventeen-observation input, five-row output, and complete explanation, five source tables, and no constraints, hints, notes, or follow-up. source_fidelity.json binds all five composed Reference files to live-content SHA-256 17eaf1a3868e7377c019d26b67fbe7bd8b0d80aa08ebef2c0d65f06b83942e45 and validates without errors.
